plugins.name: code-review
plugins.description: Structured code review and repository audit. Reviews a diff, branch or pull request against correctness, security, performance and accessibility, and reports findings ranked by severity with a concrete failure scenario for each. Use when asked to review code, audit a PR, or check quality before merging.

plugins.name: debugger
plugins.description: Diagnoses failures down to their mechanism before changing any code. Reproduces the fault deterministically, narrows it to the smallest failing case, bisects regressions to the commit that introduced them, and proves the fix with a test that fails without it. Use when something is broken, a test fails or is flaky, behaviour regressed after a change, or a crash, stack trace or incident needs a root cause.

plugins.name: developer
plugins.description: The feature development loop: orient in the code, write a change plan, implement it in verifiable slices, run the repository's own checks, and self-review before handoff. Also covers behaviour-preserving refactors. Use when asked to implement a feature, build or add functionality, work a ticket, refactor existing code, or check that a change is finished.

plugins.name: job-hunter
plugins.description: Runs a job or contract search as a pipeline instead of a pile of tabs. Scores a posting against a declared profile and says pursue or skip with the reason, tailors the application to that one posting, and tracks every opportunity through its stages with follow-ups that come due. Use when reviewing a job ad, gig or RFP, deciding whether to apply or bid, writing a proposal, cover letter or CV variant, or asking what needs chasing in the search.

plugins.name: pair-programmer
plugins.description: Pairs on code instead of taking it over. Navigates while you drive — holding the goal, questioning decisions before they are typed, and catching the change spreading past its declared scope — or plays TDD ping-pong where the suite, not either partner, decides when a turn is over. Keeps a session journal of decisions, rejected alternatives, open questions and the next step, so the work can be paused, resumed or handed over. Use when the user wants to pair, wants a second pair of eyes while they code, asks for ping-pong or test-first pairing, or asks whether the change is still on track.

plugins.name: scrum-master
plugins.description: Backlog refinement and sprint planning against GitHub Issues. Turns raw requests into ready stories with acceptance criteria and a size, splits the ones that are too big, and builds a sprint plan with one goal and a capacity number that survives contact with reality. Use when asked to refine or groom a backlog, write a user story, add acceptance criteria, estimate work, or plan the next sprint.
